opennyai_summary.facts:
Order 
This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, for grant of anticipatory bail.
2. The applicant is apprehending his arrest in relation to Crime No.128/2025 registered at Police Station Ranjhi, District Jabalpur for the offence punishable under Section 376 and 376(2)(n) of the IPC.
opennyai_summary.12_March_2025__arguments:
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant came in contact with the prosecutrix in 2014 and thereafter the applicant and prosecutrix were in relationship till 20.06.2024 and they were in physical relation but the report was made to the police on 20.02.2025 on the ground that the applicant has developed physical relation with the prosecutrix on the false pretext of marriage and now he has refused to enter into marriage with her, therefore, the offence has been registered.
He further submits that the present applicant is a government employee and if he is arrested in such a Lakhan Lal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148250384/
1 false case, his whole service career would be ruined as such, the present applicant is entitled to get the benefit of anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, the counsel for the State has opposed the submissions made by the counsel for the applicant, read over the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and submits that when prosecutrix is alleging that is it is a case wherein physical relation was developed after giving false assurance of marriage, therefore, the offence is rightly made out and bail application deserves to be rejected.
opennyai_summary.12_March_2025__decision:
I am inclined to grant interim protection to the present applicant as both the prosecutrix and applicant are major and were in relationship since 2014 which continued upto 2024, therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.
6. It is directed that in the event of arrest, the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer/Arresting Officer of the Police Station concerned.
7. The applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 482(2) of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

opennyai_summary.issue:
10. The foremost question for adjudication is that whether the petitioner NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:2832 4 MCRC-13732-2025 was engaged in physical relation with the complainant on false pretext of marriage and thereafter her consent being obtained on misconception of facts and false promise of marriage.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
11. It is well settled principle that consent of woman with respect to Section 375 of IPC must involve an active and reasoned deliberations towards the proposed acts to establish whether the consent was Lakhan Lal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173409107/
2
vitiated by misconception of fact arising out of promise to marry, two prepositions must be established.
The promise of marriage must have been a false promise, given in bad faith and with no intention to being adhered to at the time it was given.
The false promise itself must be of immediate relevance, or bear a direct nexus to the woman's decision to engage in the sexual act.
It is also established that a breach of a promise cannot be said to be a false promise.
If we reach the conclusion that he intentionally made a fraudulent misrepresentation from the very inception and the prosecutrix gave her consent on a misconception of fact, the offence of rape under Section 375 IPC is clearly made out.
As per record and contents of FIR there is no evidence of coercion or threat or injury to the complainant.
Even if the allegation in the FIR are taken as true and correct, it does not appear from the record that the consent of the complainant was obtained against her will merely on assurance of marriage.
The narration of the complainant in the FIR does not corroborate with her conduct.
14. Therefore, the consent of complainant as defined under Section 90 of IPC also cannot be said to have been under the misconception of fact.
There is no material to substantiate inducement or misrepresentation on the part of the petitioner to secure consent of physical relation without having any intention of fulfilling said promise.
16. Taking into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, it is clearly reflected that neither in the FIR nor in the statement of the complainant, anywhere it is mentioned that when complainant refused to make physical relation then the petitioner obtained her consent on the false pretext of marriage.
Apart from that, as per the FIR the last incident occurred in June 2024,
however, the FIR was lodged in February 2025 i.e. almost eight months later.
There is no reason afforded for the delay.
17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others v. Bhajanlal and others [(1992) Supp 1 SCC 335 ]. has held as under - "102.
Therefore,
considering the facts in its entirety, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the FIR amounts to abuse of the process of law, therefore, the FIR dated 20.02.2025 registered at Police Station Ranjhi,
District Jabalpur (M.P.), bearing Crime No.128/2025 for the offences punishable under Sections 376 and 376(2)(n) of the IPC and all other consequential proceedings, stands quashed.
